item.title: Compatibility
item.description:
Release Compatibility#

This shows the compatibility of materialize-monitoring with various technologies.

It is also where changes we absorb from outside this repo are recorded — a Materialize metric rename, a Grafana schema bump, an upstream chart moving a value. For what we guarantee about our own names, and the notice you get before one changes, see Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy.

materialize-terraform-self-managed#

materialize-terraform-self-managed materialize-monitoring Clouds Observability default
v11.0.0+ 0.17.0 AWS, GCP, Azure On — enable_observability defaults to true
v10.0.0 – v10.1.1 0.12.0 – 0.15.0 AWS, GCP, Azure Off — opt-in
≤ v9.0.2 none (a vendored copy of the env-top dashboard only) — —

The Terraform module ships inside the materialize-monitoring component rather than on a version stream of its own, so one number covers both: a module ref of materialize-monitoring/vX.Y.Z installs chart X.Y.Z. There is no mapping to maintain between the two.

item.title: Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy
item.description:
Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy#

This page describes which parts of materialize-monitoring you can rely on, and how the project retires an interface before it changes.

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Semantic artifact versioning#

This repository publishes several release artifacts, and each one carries its own SemVer version. An artifact bumps its version for the following kinds of change:

item.title: Common Alerts
item.description:
Common Alerts#

These are the alerting rules the chart bundles, generated from the query registry. Each is installed only where the deployment has the capabilities it requires, and only the default set installs without being selected; see Configuring Alerting.

Rules outside the default set have not all been checked against a self-managed install. Evaluate one against the deployment before relying on it.

dev-alerts#

Alerting rules for development awareness.

Each alert here is a condition the stack has already contained: nothing is down, and there is nothing for whoever runs the deployment to fix right now. The people who can remove the cause are the ones who write the software emitting it.

item.title: Common Queries
item.description:
Common Queries#

These queries are used in various dashboards and may be a good starting point for a dashboard developer or for someone looking into particulars of a dashboard.

The underlined values in each query are placeholders, and they are editable. Click one, type your environment’s value, and every other occurrence of that placeholder on the page follows — so copying a query gives you something you can paste straight into Prometheus. Press Enter to commit an edit or Escape to discard it.

You can also set placeholders up front by naming them in this page’s URL:

?mzSqlPrefix=v2_mz_&mzNamespaceList=materialize-prod

The two directions are the same mechanism: editing in place rewrites the URL to match, so once the page reads the way you want, the address bar holds a link you can bookmark or share. Only placeholders you have changed appear there, and a customized value is underlined with a solid rather than a dashed line. Reload without the query string to get the defaults back.

item.title: List of Metrics
item.description:
List of Metrics#

This has the list of metrics which are available for usage. In many systems, only a subset of metrics get stored based on how they would be used.

Metric Tiers#

Importance is about storage, not stability: it says which metrics are worth keeping when capacity is limited, not what we promise about their names. For that, see Stability Guarantees and Deprecation Policy — in short, mz_* names come from Materialize itself and we disclose rather than freeze them.

item.title: Recorded Series
item.description:
Recorded Series#

These are the series the chart’s recording rules write, generated from the query registry. A recorded series is a metric name this repository mints, so it reads the same whatever produced the measurement underneath it. The Thanos ruler evaluates the rules and writes the results back through the alloy-gateway, so a recorded series is queryable wherever the gateway’s other metrics are.

Every ext:* series is part of the normalized layer for an external dependency. One name is recorded by each adapter that can measure it, and the flavor label names the adapter.

item.title: Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)
item.description:
Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)#

Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) extend the Kubernetes API with custom resources that can be managed with standard Kubernetes tooling. materialize-monitoring both reads custom resources — to decide what to scrape — and creates them — to provision Grafana, its datasources, and its dashboards. Either way the definitions have to exist before the main chart installs, which is why they ship in a chart of their own.

item.title: Changelog

materialize-monitoring Changelog#

materialize-monitoring (Helm chart + Terraform module) v1.6.0 (Unreleased)#

Changes Pending

materialize-monitoring (Helm chart + Terraform module) v1.5.0#

  • Find GCP load balancers by their VPC network
    • materialize-monitoring#571
    • pipeline.metrics.provider.gcp.loadBalancing.networks lists VPC networks whose passthrough load balancers to pull, external or internal, beside the forwarding rules in forwardingRules. A rule either list names is pulled. Use it for a rule that cannot be named beforehand, such as one GKE makes for a Service the same release creates. On a network that holds only the cluster, as the Terraform wrappers create it, that is the cluster’s load balancers and nothing else.
  • Add a noop profile, and let the Grafana resource be turned off
    • materialize-monitoring#572
    • Turn off the chart’s Grafana resource, and install a release that creates nothing
      • connections.grafana.enabled (default true): set it to false and the chart creates no Grafana resource in any connections.grafana.mode. Use it when no grafana-operator acts on the release, or when dashboards.config.grafana.manifest.instanceSelector points the folders and datasources at a Grafana resource you manage.
      • With connections.grafana.enabled: false, the chart refuses to render folders or datasources that still select its own instance. Turn them off, or set dashboards.config.grafana.manifest.instanceSelector.
      • profiles/noop.values.yaml: a release that creates no resources. Install with it first, then turn components on over it one tag at a time. The materialize-monitoring-crds chart is unaffected.
